content_units: Kitchen Sink Slow-Drain: Likely Causes in Your Flat
Most likely this is a   localized kitchen waste-line blockage  , not a whole-flat sewer problem. The strongest clues are:
-   Bathroom drains are normal   → blockage is probably   after the kitchen sink but before the shared stack
-   Occasional gurgling   → partial blockage or mild venting/air displacement issue
-   No sewage smell   → less likely to be a failed main drain or dry trap
-   Worsened over 3 weeks   → typical of   grease/food buildup gradually narrowing the pipe
Most likely causes, in order:
-   Grease, soap, and food residue   building up in the kitchen trap/waste pipe
-   Partial blockage in the trap or horizontal waste pipe   serving only the kitchen
-   Blocked/poorly fitted sink strainer or pop-up waste parts
-   Washing machine/dishwasher standpipe or shared kitchen waste branch   contributing buildup
- Less likely:   venting issue  ,   pipe fall/alignment problem  , or   deeper stack blockage
Safe Tenant-Level Checks and First Actions
Stay within simple, non-damaging checks and a   £25 max DIY spend  .
Step   Safe check/action   What to check   Expected result
1   Boiling-not-used; use   very hot tap water + washing-up liquid     Run for 2-3 minutes, then test drain   May improve light grease buildup
2   Remove and clean   sink strainer/basket     Food sludge, grease, debris around outlet   Faster draining if top-side restriction
3   Fill sink halfway, then use a   cup plunger     Block overflow opening with wet cloth first   Partial blockage may loosen
4   Inspect under-sink   trap/U-bend   visually   Leaks, sagging hose, heavy grease residue   Confirms likely local clog area
5   If trap has a clean-out or is easy to remove, place bucket and clean it   Fatty sludge, food paste, coffee grounds   Often solves kitchen-only slow drain
6   Check dishwasher/washing machine waste hose connection   Kinked hose or greasy shared spigot   Can restore normal flow quickly
Recommended low-cost DIY kit within budget:
-   Sink plunger:   about   £5-£10
-   Rubber gloves + old cloth/bucket:   often already on hand
- Optional:   plastic drain snake for sink waste   about   £3-£8  , but use gently
What to avoid as a tenant:
-   Caustic chemical drain cleaners   that can damage older pipework/seals and complicate landlord repairs
- Taking apart fixed plumbing beyond the   accessible trap
- Using aggressive drain rods in indoor plastic waste pipes
- Repeated boiling water into plastic fittings if you’re unsure of pipe condition
When This Needs Landlord or Plumber Escalation
Escalate promptly if any of these apply:
- You clean/plunge the trap area and the sink is   still slow or gurgling
- Water backs up into the sink when   dishwasher/washing machine   drains
- Multiple fixtures start slowing later, even if they are normal now
- You notice   leaks under the sink  , swollen cabinet panels, or loose trap fittings
- Gurgling becomes frequent, loud, or happens when other flats/appliances drain
- The blockage seems beyond the trap, in the   branch line or stack
- Your tenancy agreement says plumbing disassembly is not permitted
Professional/landlord-level likely issues:
-   Blocked branch waste line in the wall/floor
-   Shared stack partial obstruction
-   Poor venting / air admittance valve issue
-   Pipe alignment/fall problem   in older kitchen waste runs
- Recurring grease blockage requiring   mechanical clearing
Best Next Move for Your Situation
Because you’re renting and bathrooms are normal, the best sequence is:
- Try   1-2 safe checks only  : clean strainer, hot water + detergent flush, then plunge
- If accessible and you’re comfortable, clean the   trap/U-bend
- If not clearly fixed after that,   report it to the landlord/property manager
A good tenant message would be:

- “Kitchen sink has been draining slowly for 3 weeks and now occasionally gurgles. Bathroom drains are normal. I’ve cleaned the strainer and checked for simple blockage, so it may be in the kitchen waste line beyond the trap.”
